title: Lesson 27 - OmniScript Element Selection: Steps, Blocks, and Inputs
description: Recommend the proper components to be used to respond to business needs (Steps, Blocks, Inputs, Display Functions, Formulas, etc.).

questions.question: An OmniScript must collect a list of line items, each with a product, quantity, and price. What is the correct element structure?
options: A single Step with one text Input for the whole list
A repeatable Block containing product, quantity, and price Inputs
Three separate Steps, one per field
questions.explanation: A list of line items is a repeating group, so a repeatable Block is the right structure: each instance holds product, quantity, and price, and writes to its own data JSON node. A single text input cannot hold structured line items, separate Steps fragment the task, and a read-only input cannot capture data.

questions.question: A consultant needs to show a fetched account name to the user for confirmation, but the user should not edit it. What element should be used?
options: A read-only Input that displays the value from the data JSON
questions.explanation: A read-only Input displays a value from the data JSON without allowing edits, which is exactly the confirmation use case. An editable input invites changes, a repeatable Block is for lists, and a picklist is for a fixed set of choices.

questions.question: Two Inputs in an OmniScript are accidentally given the same data JSON name. What is the result?
options: The two Inputs collide and one overwrites the other in the data JSON
Both values are stored in an array
The second Input is ignored silently
questions.explanation: The data JSON name is the contract, and two Inputs with the same name collide, with one overwriting the other. This corrupts the data the downstream logic reads. Names must be unique and deliberate.
